common_name: Green Comet Milkweed / Green-flowered Milkweed / Wand Milkweed
look_here_first: Start with the inflorescence position and flower color. Green comet milkweed has tight greenish flower clusters, often from upper leaf axils, with hoods/corona held compactly; leaves are opposite and relatively broad, and the plant lacks the bright green-white spreading flower look of A. viridis.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Natural Purola flora lists A. viridiflora as naturally occurring. Travis — UT herbarium index includes A. viridiflora. Williamson — county flora includes A. viridiflora.

best_field_traits: hoods shorter and more compact than in A. viridis
follicles slender and erect to ascending
morphology_keys.comparison_training: A. viridis has larger green-and-white flowers with broad spreading reflexed corolla lobes and more prominent pale hoods. A. viridiflora is more uniformly greenish and compact-flowered.

photo_strategy.target_count: 2 core views now; add fruit and flower-macro variants later if diagnostically useful
photo_strategy.visual_priority: compact greenish upper-axillary inflorescence + local voucher architecture
photo_strategy.comparison_note: Teach against A. viridis by compact, more uniformly greenish flowers versus larger green-and-white spreading flowers.
